  "text": "The laundrette on Bell Street had six machines, though the one nearest the door had been out of order since May.

Ruth came on Tuesdays with a blue bag and enough coins for washing, but not drying. She took her clothes home damp and hung them above the bath.

The attendant usually stayed behind a plywood partition, listening to horse racing.

One wet afternoon, he came out carrying a spider plant.

“Would you know what’s wrong with this?”

Ruth touched a brown leaf.

“How often do you water it?”

“When I remember.”

“And when’s that?”

He considered.

“Saturdays, mostly.”

She tipped the pot. Water spilled onto her shoe.

“Skip a Saturday.”

The next week the plant stood on top of the broken machine, on a folded towel. Someone had cut away the brown leaves.

“Looking better,” Ruth said.

“Early days.”

In October, she found a small cutting beside her usual machine. Its roots floated in a mustard jar.

“For your bathroom,” the attendant said.

“I didn’t say I had a window.”

“Have you?”

“Yes.”

“Well, then.”

She carried it home inside an empty washing-powder box.

By January it needed a larger pot. Ruth brought the jar back, washed, with three biscuits wrapped in foil inside.

The attendant took one and offered her another.

“They’re yours,” she said.

“I know.”

They ate standing beside the machines while a zip clicked against a glass door.

Before leaving, Ruth looked at the original plant. A slender stem had reached down almost to the coin slot.

“You’ll have to move that when they fix the machine.”

The attendant brushed crumbs from his shirt.

“Plenty of time.”"
